compiled_state.description:
## Context

The noun-based `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` surface now exists. This ticket
makes that vocabulary primary across the CLI, reconciler engine, workflow, scripts, tests, and
documentation. It is an additive expand-contract migration: existing workflows and environments
that still invoke `rebar reconcile`, engine `--mode`, or `--filter-local-ids` must continue to
work with their existing behavior.

The compatibility layer cannot be a naive alias to `bridge sync`. The existing defaults differ:

- `rebar reconcile` with no arguments is dry-run because the CLI wrapper injects
  `--mode dry-run`.
- `python -m rebar_reconciler` with no arguments defaults to live.
- `rebar.reconcile()` defaults to dry-run.
- `rebar bridge sync` with no arguments mutates.

The old entrypoints therefore remain explicit adapters that preserve their own defaults and map
onto the same core planning/execution path. New help, generated references, workflows, scripts,
and runbooks use the bridge vocabulary. The legacy spellings may be hidden from primary help, but
invoking them remains supported. Any future removal requires a separate deprecation decision after
real consumers have migrated; removal is not part of this epic.

## Surface scope and compatibility boundaries

This story makes the CLI and engine bridge vocabulary primary while retaining CLI/engine
compatibility. The public library `rebar.reconcile(mode=...)` and MCP `reconcile(mode=...)`
remain callable at this boundary; sibling `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` adds bridge-shaped library and MCP
operations and must retain the old operations as compatibility entrypoints too.

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py` survives. `MODE_CAPS` and the `Mode` ladder are
still required by:

- legacy `--mode` compatibility;
- the MCP compatibility surface until and after `f789`;
- the phase gate, whose rollback-safe value `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` must remain a real
  `Mode` member so unknown-value handling cannot fail open.

The engine parser accepts both the primary subcommand vocabulary and legacy flags. Both routes
normalize into one internal request before lock acquisition or pass execution; the compatibility
path does not fork state, gate, retry, exit, or mutation policy.

`--filter-local-ids` also remains accepted on the legacy path with its existing write-filter
semantics. In-tree callers migrate to `--only`, which intentionally narrows examination as well
as writes, but the old flag must not silently acquire the stronger `--only` semantics for
external callers.

## Workflow rollback-brake migration

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` currently runs
`rebar reconcile --mode "$MODE"`. Migrate the workflow and its `workflow_dispatch` input to the
new vocabulary in the same change:

- `reconcile-check` -> retained `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check` (lock-free diagnostic)
- `dry-run` -> `rebar bridge preview`
- `bootstrap-strict` -> `bridge sync --max-changes 10`
- `bootstrap-throttle` -> `bridge sync --max-changes 100`
- `live` -> `bridge sync`
- stop entirely -> durable `bridge pause` from `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19`

This keeps the production rollback brake continuously available. The old workflow invocation
remains valid for older checked-out workflow revisions and self-hosted environments.

## Direct callers and references

Migrate both pressure-test scripts from engine `--mode` to primary `preview` / `sync`
subcommands and from `--filter-local-ids` to `--only` where their intent is to bound the entire
validation probe:

- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_validation_probe.sh`
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`

Migrate the engine tests and external Jira helpers rather than deleting them:

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py`
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_filter.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`

Primary documentation moves to `bridge preview` / `bridge sync`, while release/migration notes
document the retained compatibility entrypoints and their distinct defaults.

## Test plan

Build a behavioral parity matrix through real CLI and direct engine entrypoints. For every legacy
mode, prove the old invocation and its new primary equivalent produce the same observable plan,
mutation boundary, cap, output class, and exit status. Explicitly prove the two defaults do not
collapse: argument-less `rebar reconcile` stays dry-run, argument-less direct engine invocation
stays live, and argument-less `rebar bridge sync` stays mutating.

Exercise representative phase-gated, paused, in-flight, invalid-argument, and filtered-ID outcomes
through both vocabularies. Prove `--filter-local-ids` retains its legacy write-only filtering
contract while `--only` narrows examination, so compatibility is not implemented by a
behavior-changing flag rename.

Parse and execute the production workflow command-selection block for every dispatch value and
prove the rollback mapping above. Grep shipped workflows, scripts, primary help, and current docs
for stale primary invocations, with explicit exclusions for compatibility registration/tests,
release and migration notes, CHANGELOG, archived docs, and ADR history.

Surface parity census:

- CLI: in scope; new and legacy spellings are exercised through `rebar`.
- Direct engine: in scope; subcommands and legacy flags are exercised through
  `python -m rebar_reconciler`.
- Library: continuity control only; `rebar.reconcile(...)` remains callable and behaviorally
  unchanged. New bridge library operations belong to `f789`.
- MCP: continuity control only; the existing `reconcile` tool remains callable. New bridge MCP
  operations belong to `f789`.
- Automated callers: in scope through the real workflow selection block, pressure-test scripts,
  external Jira helpers, and generated/current documentation.
- Dual direction: in scope; preview remains non-mutating and sync/mapped live modes remain mutating.

No new contention harness is required because both vocabularies normalize before the existing
single pass/lock seams and add no retry, cache, or composed write operation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` are the primary documented CLI spellings
      and route through the reconciler engine's primary subcommand vocabulary.
- [x] `rebar reconcile` remains functional as a compatibility entrypoint. With no arguments it
      remains dry-run; every existing `--mode` value retains its prior observable behavior.
- [x] Direct `python -m rebar_reconciler --mode ...` and argument-less engine invocations remain
      functional with their prior defaults, while primary `preview` / `sync` subcommands route
      to the same normalized core request.
- [x] Legacy `--filter-local-ids` remains accepted with its prior write-filter semantics;
      primary `--only` keeps its narrower examination contract. Tests prove they are not silently
      treated as identical.
- [x] `mode.py`, `MODE_CAPS`, and the `Mode` ladder remain available, and the phase gate can
      round-trip `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` as a real `Mode` member.
- [x] The library `rebar.reconcile(...)` and MCP `reconcile` tool remain callable and unchanged
      at this ticket boundary.
- [x] `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` and its `workflow_dispatch` inputs use the new
      vocabulary with the exact rollback-brake mapping above; the old command still works when run
      by an older workflow revision.
- [x] Both pressure-test scripts and external Jira helpers use the new primary vocabulary, while
      behavioral compatibility tests retain coverage of the old engine flags.
- [x] A real-entrypoint parity matrix proves old and new spellings match for mapped success,
      failure, gate, pause, in-flight, cap, output, and exit behavior without changing the distinct
      no-argument defaults.
- [x] Every primary help string avoids internal vocabulary (mode, rank, gate, lock, cap, pass,
      binding store, or raw exit-code numbers); compatibility/migration help states the old-to-new
      mapping without changing behavior.
- [x] Current docs and generated reference use `bridge preview` / `bridge sync`; release notes
      document the mapping, retained compatibility, and distinct legacy defaults.
- [x] Legacy CLI, direct-engine, library, MCP, workflow, and external-helper callers using `reconcile`, `--mode`, or `--filter-local-ids` retain their documented entrypoints, defaults, and write-filter semantics, proven by the compatibility suites named in this plan.

## File impact

- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`: make bridge preview/sync primary; retain the reconcile adapter and
  its dry-run default.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`: add/normalize primary subcommands; retain
  `--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and the direct-engine live default.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mode.py`: compatibility and phase-gate continuity control;
  must remain.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`: make bridge vocabulary primary and document migration.
- `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`: migrate production invocation and rollback input
  without invalidating old workflow revisions.
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_validation_probe.sh`: migrate primary invocation.
- `scripts/jira-pressure-test/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`: migrate primary invocation.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py`: primary and compatibility
  entrypoint parity.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_filter.py`: distinct legacy/new filter
  semantics.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/_dc_support.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`,
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_user_guide_commands.py`: migrate primary test callers while
  retaining compatibility coverage.
- `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`, and
  `docs/release-notes.md`: primary vocabulary plus compatibility/migration contract.
## Route ownership and plan-review remediation

This story owns the concrete route signal: canonical `rebar bridge preview` / `bridge sync` launch the engine with primary `preview` / `sync` subcommands, while `rebar reconcile`, `rebar.reconcile()`, MCP `reconcile`, and direct-engine compatibility callers continue to invoke legacy `--mode`. `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py` therefore changes the canonical bridge launcher without collapsing the legacy `launch_reconciler` adapter or its dry-run default.

This story migrates the production workflow invocation but deliberately retains its existing numeric compatibility mapping. Dependent story `9895-aa2c-8907-4db6` lands after this story, centralizes semantic dispositions, and only then deletes the canonical workflow numeric whitelist. Older workflow revisions keep invoking `rebar reconcile --mode` and continue to receive their historical codes.

Additional proving/edit targets are `src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge.txt`, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py`, and `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py`. The workflow oracle must preserve paused-marker commit-skip plus the legacy rc mapping while asserting the new invocation selection; the real CLI oracle must prove primary subcommands and compatibility defaults through subprocesses.
## Operational flag mechanics (plan-review remediation)

The primary engine parser is an additive normalized-request layer. Because `__main__.py` is near the 800-line hard cap, parser construction and normalization move along their existing call seam into a new `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py` module. It produces one request carrying route (`preview`, `sync`, or legacy `--mode`), optional `max_changes`, optional `only`, optional `except`, and the retained legacy `filter_local_ids`. The old argument-less engine route still normalizes to legacy live; `rebar reconcile` still injects legacy dry-run.

`--max-changes N` is a NEW canonical sync flag. The bridge `sync` subparser accepts and forwards a positive integer. The engine threads `max_changes` through `run_pass` and `reconcile_once` into the existing applier partition seam. `apply_planning._partition_by_mode_cap` uses the explicit cap when present and otherwise uses the retained `MODE_CAPS` value. It never rewrites `Mode` or `MODE_CAPS`. Therefore `bridge sync --max-changes 10` and `100` reproduce bootstrap-strict and bootstrap-throttle mutation caps while legacy `--mode bootstrap-strict` / `bootstrap-throttle` remain byte-for-byte valid for old callers. Invalid, zero, or negative values fail as invocation errors before lock or mutation.

`--only IDS` and `--except IDS` are NEW canonical preview/sync selection flags and are mutually exclusive. They accept non-empty comma-separated local IDs or bound Jira keys. Before lock inspection or acquisition, a read-only selection preflight resolves every supplied local ID or bound Jira key to a stable local-ID set. The preflight reuses `_read_local_tickets(repo_root, no_sync=True)` plus `binding_store.load_binding_store(repo_root)`; both reads avoid ticket-branch sync, snapshot writes, and lock-ref writes. Empty, wholly unresolved, and partially unresolved selections return invocation error 2 at this point. The normalized request then carries only the resolved local-ID set. After the ordinary full snapshots and binding store are loaded under the pass lock but BEFORE any differ runs, the engine uses that already-resolved set to narrow `local_tickets`, `prev_snapshot`, and `curr_snapshot`: `--only` keeps the selected set and `--except` removes it. It does not resolve user input a second time. The existing legacy `--filter-local-ids` path remains separate and unchanged: all differs see full inputs, then only matching mutations reach the applier. Tests must prove the two mechanisms are observably distinct and that neither flag changes unrelated repository/ref state.

Selection helpers live in the existing `reconcile_helpers.py` call-graph seam so `reconcile.py` and `__main__.py` remain below the hard module cap. The explicit cap is passed through `reconcile.py` to `applier.py`, with partition behavior implemented in `apply_planning.py`; no retry, cache, or new lock is introduced.

The existing external-DC `run_reconcile(mode, only=...)` helper remains a LEGACY compatibility helper and keeps mapping to `--mode` plus post-differ `--filter-local-ids`. Its consumers `_dc_fixtures.py`, `test_dc_mutations.py`, and `test_store_copy_isolation.py` are intentionally unchanged and stay compatibility coverage. A separate additive `run_bridge(...)` helper is used only by explicitly migrated primary-path tests. `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` remains in the proving set to pin the old reconcile interception/dry-run default and gains canonical dispatch coverage.

## Additional acceptance proof

- [x] `bridge sync --max-changes 10` and `100` apply exactly 10 and 100 deterministic mutations, defer the remainder, and leave legacy bootstrap mode caps unchanged; invalid caps exit 2 before lock or mutation.
- [x] `bridge preview/sync --only` and `--except` narrow examination before every differ, while legacy `--filter-local-ids` still post-filters writes after full examination; real-entrypoint tests prove distinct plans and unchanged unrelated state.
- [x] The legacy external-DC helper and all three named consumers retain `--mode` / `--filter-local-ids` behavior; additive primary helpers do not silently migrate compatibility fixtures.
The shipped repository census keeps `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` operator guidance on `rebar bridge preview`, while compatibility fixtures, historical ADRs, release/migration notes, and explicit old-workflow tests retain the legacy spelling where they prove continuity.
## Reconcile-check continuity correction

The workflow mapping above is authoritative: `reconcile-check` is NOT a synonym for preview. it is the retained lock-free diagnostic branch, writes `bridge_state/reconcile-check.json`, and intentionally bypasses the ordinary snapshot/pass path. Until a separately specified primary verb carries that exact diagnostic contract, the production workflow maps only `dry-run` to `rebar bridge preview`; its `reconcile-check` dispatch value continues to invoke `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check`. This explicit compatibility use is allowed in the primary workflow because changing it would break the rollback/safe-first-run contract.

The parity matrix compares every legacy mode with a primary equivalent only where semantics are truly equivalent. It proves reconcile-check unchanged through the retained legacy workflow branch, including no pass-lock acquisition, no snapshot mutation, the same diagnostic artifact/output class, and the same exit behavior. No new primary command claims to replace reconcile-check in this story.

- [x] The migrated production workflow keeps its reconcile-check selection on `rebar reconcile --mode reconcile-check`; dry-run alone maps to `bridge preview`; tests prove the lock-free diagnostic artifact and every old checked-out workflow remain unchanged.
## Capped-sync deferred-output contract

A capped canonical sync must preserve the rollback-brake audit surface, not merely truncate writes. When `target_mode` is LIVE and explicit `max_changes` is present, `apply_planning._emit_mode_manifest` uses a NEW capped-LIVE branch: it keeps the existing deterministic `_mode_sort_key` ordering, writes and RETAINS the normal manifest, records `max_changes`, lists the full `deferred` remainder (including an empty list when the explicit ceiling is not reached), and returns the manifest path/output class used by capped legacy modes. The presence of an explicit cap, not whether deferral happened, selects this retained audit contract. Uncapped LIVE behavior is unchanged: its temporary manifest is deleted and the applied/failed tally is returned exactly as before. Legacy bootstrap modes and their manifest shapes remain unchanged.

The cap oracle seeds 102 deterministically ordered candidate mutations. `--max-changes 10` and `100` exercise deferral and assert exact applied identifiers, counts 10/100, deferred counts 92/2, retained manifest path, and unchanged unrelated repository/ref state. `--max-changes 200` exercises an explicit ceiling above the workset and asserts all 102 apply, `deferred == []`, and the audit manifest is still retained. A mutation that removes the explicit-cap branch must make these oracles fail.

- [x] Capped LIVE sync retains a manifest with exact deterministic applied/deferred partitions (10/92 and 100/2 from a 102-mutation fixture) and also retains it with 102/0 when an explicit cap of 200 is not reached; uncapped LIVE still deletes its temporary manifest, and legacy bootstrap output remains unchanged.

Any supplied identifier in `--only` or `--except` that does not resolve to an existing local ID or bound Jira key is an invocation error before lock or mutation, even when other supplied identifiers resolve. The engine never silently substitutes a partially resolved subset. The parity matrix includes mixed known/unknown selections for both flags and asserts rc 2 plus zero repository/ref change.


## Subject identity and exact canonical forwarding

This plan is the plan for story `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` itself. It is the downstream
flag-owning story that prerequisite `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a` names; there is no second story
competing for ownership. The current absence of `--max-changes`, `--only`, and `--except`
is the forward-looking implementation gap this story closes, not an assertion that those
capabilities already exist. The parent epic commits four surviving operational flags across the verb set. This story owns
the three preview/sync flags: `--max-changes`, `--only`, and `--except`. The fourth flag,
`--max-age`, belongs to `bridge status` story `b69c-5787-81b8-4052`; that ticket explicitly
requires canonical `bridge status` and compatibility `bridge-status` to share `--max-age`.
Prerequisite `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a` is corrected to reflect this verb-level ownership.

The canonical route is built in this change before any workflow uses it:
`_bridge_commands._parser` adds the preview/sync child options; `bridge_cli` serializes the
validated namespace into engine argv; and `_launch_bridge_command` calls
`launch_reconciler((command, *child_argv), default_mode=None)`. The launcher is widened so it
injects `--mode` only when a legacy adapter supplies a non-null `default_mode`; otherwise it
forwards canonical `preview` or `sync` plus child options unchanged. New engine
`request.py` parses either shape into one normalized request before lock acquisition.

Consequently `rebar bridge sync --max-changes 10` reaches normalized
`request.max_changes == 10` and uses live behavior with an explicit cap, while legacy
`rebar reconcile --mode bootstrap-strict` still reaches `Mode.BOOTSTRAP_STRICT` and the
existing `MODE_CAPS` path. The workflow is migrated in the same Gerrit change only after
this parser, forwarding, normalization, partition, and retained-manifest behavior exists, so
the workflow never relies on a capability presumed to predate this story.

## Selection preflight ordering correction

The pre-lock resolver is an explicit new call seam in this story. `request.py` performs
syntax and non-empty checks, then `__main__.py` calls a selection resolver in
`reconcile_helpers.py` before `check_pass_lock`, the phase gate, or
`acquire_pass_lock`. That resolver reads local tickets with `no_sync=True`, opens the
binding store read-only, requires every token to map to an existing local ID, and returns
only local IDs. A local ID is valid only when present in the read ticket set; a Jira key is
valid only when `BindingStore.get_local_id` maps it to such a ticket. Any missing token,
including one missing member of a mixed list, returns 2 without a lock ref, ticket sync,
snapshot update, or mutation.

The pass receives this resolved set. After its normal locked snapshot/binding load, it
narrows all three differ inputs before invoking any differ. This deliberately performs one
small read-only preflight plus the existing pass load: it does not fetch Jira or duplicate
snapshot construction before the lock. Tests instrument `check_pass_lock`,
`acquire_pass_lock`, the fetcher, and repository/ref snapshots to prove unresolved input
returns before every one of those effects.

## Durable architecture record

This story adds `docs/adr/0092-bridge-primary-vocabulary-compatibility-adapters.md` and its
`docs/adr/.numbers/0092` reservation, then regenerates `docs/adr/README.md`. If 0092 is
claimed on the mandatory pre-push refresh, the change takes the next available number and
regenerates the index rather than colliding.

The ADR records why the expand-contract migration uses explicit legacy adapters over one
normalized request instead of aliases: `reconcile`, direct engine invocation, library
`reconcile`, and `bridge sync` have different historical defaults; legacy
`--filter-local-ids` is a post-differ write filter while canonical selection is pre-differ;
and `reconcile-check` is a lock-free diagnostic rather than preview. It also records the
capped-LIVE retained-manifest decision, the separately preserved uncapped/legacy behavior,
and the later-removal precondition that real consumers first migrate under a separate
deprecation decision. Release notes and the architecture documentation link to the ADR.

- [x] The ADR, collision-proof number marker, generated ADR index, and architecture/release
      links durably capture the distinct-default adapter and capped-manifest rationale; the ADR
      number checker and generated-index check pass.

## Library and MCP continuity proof

The affected gate explicitly runs `tests/interfaces/facades/test_library.py` and
`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp.py` as compatibility controls. The MCP suite invokes
`srv.call_tool("reconcile", {"mode": "dry-run"})` through the real MCP facade and pins
read-only, mutating-mode refusal, and invalid-mode behavior; the library suite pins the
public `rebar.reconcile` surface. These existing tests are not rewritten to canonical
bridge vocabulary because their purpose in this story is to prove that the old public
entrypoints remain callable and retain their defaults while the shared engine gains its
normalized request path.

- [x] The named library and MCP facade suites pass unchanged and prove legacy
      `rebar.reconcile` plus MCP `reconcile(mode=...)` remain callable with historical
      gating/default behavior.

## Max-age verb ownership correction

`--max-age` is not a preview/sync selector and no such existing engine flag is claimed here.
It is the stale-liveness assertion on `bridge status`, already specified and tested by
`b69c-5787-81b8-4052`. Keeping it with status ensures both the canonical and restored legacy
status spellings accept identical options. This story neither invents a duplicate sync
`--max-age` nor leaves the epic flag unowned.

## Selection staleness under the pass lock

A token that resolved during the read-only preflight can become stale before the pass finishes
loading its locked inputs because ticket events do not use the reconciler pass lock. After the
normal locked load produces `local_tickets`, the engine compares every preflight-resolved local
ID with that loaded local-ID set before invoking any differ. If any target disappeared, both
`--only` and `--except` fail closed with invocation code 2 and a stale-selection diagnostic
naming the missing IDs; the finally path releases the pass lock. No differ, Jira mutation,
binding/snapshot persistence, or manifest emission runs. It does not silently intersect to an
empty selection and does not reinterpret the original token.

The held-out oracle simulates a target present during preflight and absent from the locked load,
then asserts rc 2, the diagnostic, lock release, and zero calls to every differ/applier/persist
seam.

      differ, applier, or persistence seam; removing the under-lock recheck fails the held-out
      oracle.
